newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firm after sharp fall on Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firm after sharp fall on Yeltsin.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds recovered some ground from in nervous trading on Monday but were still well below Friday's levels after a top surgeon said President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery could be delayed or cancelled, dealers said.

Renat Akchurin, the doctor chosen to carry out the planned bypass operation on Yeltsin, said on Sunday that the 65-year-old leader could wait another 1-1/2 to two months and might have to resign himself to not having it.
Prices fell up to two figures in early trading with selling fuelled by pessimistic newspaper comment about Yeltsin's health, dealers said.
But the fall of the third, fourth and fifth tranches stopped at support levels of 75.50-75.80, 49.10-49.40 and 31.15-31.45 respectively, they added.
The sixth and seventh tranches are less liquid inside Russia, while the 2003 and 2008 maturities were the most actively traded today, dealers said.
"The reaction to the (newspaper) comments was exaggerated and the market is catching up now," Eurobank dealer Olivier Coursault said. But it was premature to speak of a recovery.
"The market is really nervous... It can go any way with news about Yeltsin," he said.
Dealers said prices were unlikely to rise more as the market awaited further political and medical news from the Kremlin.
"Prices are rising back now but it is unlikely to last long. It could all be just position-closing," Avtobank dealer Alla Zakharova said.
"Every bank has its own strategy and those foreign banks who were selling actively in the morning are bidding high now," she added.
